# Rear sway bar removal and installation

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Locate rear sway bar on back of car running along axle. [t1260]

Remove the rear sway bar links and secure or remove end brackets if they obstruct parts. [t1260]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Locate the rear sway bar on the back of the car running along the axle.
2. [Partial] Soak the hardware with PB Blaster and leave it for a couple days, repeating this process three times over about a week if stuck.
3. PB Blast the specific bolts circled in the reference picture while ignoring the bolt marked by an arrow.
4. [Partial] Detach both tie rod ends with a 14mm socket on the nut while securing the frame bracket head against rotation using a 14mm open-end spanner.
5. Loosen the top bolt on the axle clamp for both sides of the sway bar.
6. Completely remove the bottom bolt on the axle clamp for both sides of the sway bar.

_Procedure reported by [t1260]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-remove-rear-sway-bar.2814/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1260] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the rear sway bar links to detach the anti-roll bar from the chassis.
2. Secure or remove the end brackets attached directly to the axle if they obstruct other parts.

</details>

## Tools

- [Partial] 14mm socket wrench [t1260]
- [Partial] 14mm open-end wrench [t1260]
- 14 mm wrench [t1260]
- [Partial] Socket handle with 2 ft pipe extension (optional) [t1260]
- Angle grinder with cutoff wheel [t1260]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use anti-seize compound on reinstalled bolts in the axle bracket to plug holes and prevent rusting. [t1260]
- [Partial] Note that tie ends require holding the bolt head while removing the nut, whereas top clamp bolts only need loosening due to their slot placement. [t1260]
- [Partial] Use a zip tie to secure the open end of the 14 mm wrench to the down strut for better leverage. [t1260]
- [Partial] Apply a long pipe over the socket handle to break stubborn bolts free. [t1260]

## Common mistakes

- Failing to remove axle brackets that interfere with other components like rear trusses. [t1260]
